citation: Konstantopoulos, S., Li, W., Miller, S. R., & van der Ploeg, A. (2016). Effects of interim assessments across the achievement distribution: Evidence from an experiment. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 76(4), 587-608. https://doi.org/10.1177/0013164415606498
report_number: IES grant R305E090005 (Indiana diagnostic/interim assessments cluster RCT). EPM 76(4):587-608.
design: Cluster RCT; assignment level = School; 59 K-8 schools randomly assigned (35 treatment / 24 control), ITT sample of 57 schools that provided data, treatment-received (TOT) sample of 50 schools (K-2 subset 44 schools that administered Terra Nova); ~25,000 students; subjects = mathematics & reading; grades K-8 (analyzed by band: K-2 mCLASS, 3-8 Acuity). Outcome = business-as-usual control (control schools had no access to mCLASS/Acuity or their trainings).
problems: WHICH 2016 PAPER: There are TWO Konstantopoulos-et-al.-2016 papers from the SAME IES R305E090005 Indiana mCLASS/Acuity RCT: (a) THIS one, Educational and Psychological Measurement 76(4):587-608, DOI 10.1177/0013164415606498 (legal green OA author-manuscript on PubMed Central PMC5965570 / Europe PMC); and (b) Konstantopoulos, Miller, van der Ploeg & Li (2016), 'Effects of Interim Assessments on Student Achievement,' Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness 9(1):188-208, DOI 10.1080/19345747.2015.1116031, which is CLOSED/paywalled (OpenAlex is_oa=false oa_status=closed; Unpaywall returns no OA location). The JREE paper is the one that reports plain mean/OLS ITT treatment effects per grade band and is the more natural SMD source, but it has NO legal OA copy, so it could not be used. I extracted from the OA EPM paper instead. CONSEQUENCE / KEY CAVEAT: the EPM paper reports ONLY QUANTILE-REGRESSION treatment effects (10th/25th/50th/75th/90th percentiles); it does NOT report an OLS mean coefficient. The values extracted below are the 50th-quantile (MEDIAN) treatment effects, used as the best available proxy for the standardized mean difference. A median quantile effect is NOT identical to the mean SMD the meta-analysis used; the numbers will differ (likely modestly) from the JREE mean ITT estimates. The outcome was z-standardized WITHIN grade (mean=0, SD=1, grade-specific SD), so each quantile coefficient is already a standardized difference in SD units (=d); Hedges J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = N_students-2 is ~1.0000 at these large samples, so g ~= d. SEs are cluster-corrected for between-school variability (cluster_adjusted=true); ICC not reported as a single design-effect value, so icc=null (never guessed). Per-arm n_t/n_c not separately reported (only total student N per band and school counts 35T/24C assigned, 32T/18C received), so n_t/n_c=null. ROW-62 (K-2) LIMITATION: Table 3 (ITT) does NOT include a K-2 grade band (K-2 / mCLASS analyses appear only in Table 4 TOT and the single-grade IV Tables 6-7). Therefore the K-2 contrasts (row 62) below use the TOT analysis (Table 4), NOT ITT, and so may be slightly biased relative to the ITT estimates used for row 61; the K-2 TOT effects are essentially zero / not significant in either subject. ROW-61 (3-6) uses ITT Table 3 'Grades 3 to 6' rows (the registry 3-6 band; the broader 'Grades 3 to 8' ITT median estimates are Math 0.175*/SE 0.074 and Reading 0.060/SE 0.042, very similar). pretest_adjusted=false for all four (Tables 3-4 control for student+school covariates but NOT prior achievement; prior-score sensitivity models exist only for single grades 4-6, IV only, Table 7). TerraNova (K-2) and ISTEP+ (3-8) are both independent standardized tests (CTB/McGraw-Hill). Math -> STEM, Reading -> Reading per spec.

effect_sizes.test_name: ISTEP+ mathematics (Indiana state test); z-standardized within grade
effect_sizes.g_method: Outcome z-standardized within grade (SD=1), so the treatment quantile coefficient is already a standardized difference (d=0.176). 50th-quantile (median) ITT treatment effect used as proxy for the mean SMD. Hedges J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1), df = N_students-2 = 12587, J=0.99994; g = J*d = 0.17599; g_se = J*0.063 = 0.063; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.003969.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.597, Table 3 (Quantile Regression Estimates, ITT; Grades 3 to 6, Mathematics 50th quantile: 0.176*, SE 0.063, schools=57, students=12,589)
effect_sizes.notes: MEDIAN (50th-quantile) ITT treatment effect, NOT an OLS mean (paper reports only quantile estimates). Statistically significant (p<=.05). Total students with ISTEP+ math in 3-6 band = 12,589 across 57 schools; per-arm n not reported. Lower-tail estimates larger (10th=0.214*, 25th=0.205*); upper tail 75th=0.155*, 90th=0.172*. Broader 'Grades 3-8' ITT median = 0.175* (SE 0.074). TOT 3-6 median = 0.192* (Table 4); IV 3-6 median = 0.177* (Table 5). Acuity (grades 3-8) is the interim-assessment program with associated teacher training ('TPD for curricula' descriptor).

effect_sizes.notes: MEDIAN (50th-quantile) TOT treatment effect (mCLASS). NO ITT K-2 row exists in the paper (Table 3 ITT omits K-2); K-2 appears only in TOT Table 4 and single-grade IV Tables 6-7, so this is TOT not ITT. Not statistically significant at any quantile (all K-2 estimates ns). Total K-2 TerraNova math students = 7,517 across 44 schools (only 44 of 50 schools administered TerraNova); per-arm n not reported. Authors conclude mCLASS had no significant K-2 effect, possibly due to TerraNova-mCLASS misalignment. Single-grade IV (Table 6) math medians: K=0.032, G1=-0.028, G2=0.027 (all ns).
